payload.markdown: This is not going to convince anyone who is not already convinced, but to me object-oriented code is aesthetically pleasing. The messiness of implementation is hidden away behind clean interfaces, making an object a thing of apparent simplicity to its client.

blocks.text: This is not going to convince anyone who is not already convinced, but to me object-oriented code is aesthetically pleasing. The messiness of implementation is hidden away behind clean interfaces, making an object a thing of apparent simplicity to its client.

payload.markdown: I love the neatness and elegance of polymorphism, so that an API allows you to manipulate vastly different objects that nonetheless perform interchangeably and transparently—the way that objects can be stacked up neatly or slotted into one another like children’s blocks. Of course, there are those who argue that the converse is true. Object-oriented code can manifest itself as an explosion of classes all so decoupled from one another that piecing together their relationships can be a headache. This is a code smell in its own right. It is often tempting to build factories that produce factories that produce factories, until your code resembles a hall of mirrors. Sometimes it makes sense to do the simplest thing that works and then refactor in just enough elegance for testing and flexibility. Let the problem space determine your solution rather than a list of best practices.

payload.text: Note The rigid application of so-called best practice is also often an issue in project management. Whenever the use of a technique or a process begins to resemble ritual, applied automatically and inflexibly, it’s worth taking a moment to investigate the reasoning behind your current approach. It could be you’re drifting from the realm of tools to that of the cargo cult.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
HTTP & REST: Designing HTTP endpoints as resources with predictable methods and status codes.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Polymorphism: Different classes responding to the same call each in their own way.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
CLI Tools: Running PHP from the terminal: plain scripts, Composer scripts and REPL tools.
Git, CI & Build: Version control plus automated checks that run on every change.
